requiredPatches.reason: Actual Swift 6 error at main.swift:43: a nonisolated global function cannot mutate the main-actor-isolated top-level var. Replacing the global function with a non-escaping closure literal at the call site keeps the closure inside the main actor's isolation (it runs synchronously inside make, which the main actor calls), so no @MainActor annotation, nonisolated(unsafe), shared mutable state or checking suppression is needed. Emitted lines, stage collection, setup-only report and all protocol behaviour are unchanged.

validationRequirements: Static analysis only; nothing was compiled here. Rebuild the frozen package copy and the worktree: the CLI target must compile with strict Swift 6 concurrency checking unchanged and no new warnings in this file.

If the compiler instead reports that the closure 'loses global actor' or must be Sendable, that would indicate the installed toolchain treats the parameter as escaping or Sendable; in that case the only acceptable follow-up is to re-verify that RMSCoscheduleSetup.make declares emit as a plain non-escaping (String) -> Void, which the pasted signature confirms. Do not add nonisolated(unsafe) or disable checking.

Behaviour must be identical to the previous intent: every 'setup stage done:' line still appends its stage name to the collector in order; --setup-only writes the setup report, prints the summary and END, exits 0 only when setupCompleted; normal mode calls run exactly as before.
rms-coschedule-pure-tests are untouched by this patch and must still report 60 passed, 0 failed.
